name: Ava: Transcribe Voice to Text
oneLine: Live captioning app for deaf and hard of hearing people, with group conversations, offline mode, sound alerts and optional human captioners.

platforms.text: iPhone, iPad, Android, web, Windows, Mac
platforms.detail: Mobile apps for iOS and Android, a web app and a desktop app for Windows and Mac.

deviceRequirements.detail: The current App Store version (October 2026) needs iOS 18.6 or later; Ava's help centre still lists iOS 15.0. Android needs version 10 or later.

roomCaptions.detail: Ava uses the phone's microphone to caption the person you are talking to, and captions start when you open the app.

groupConversations.text: Up to 25 people, each on their own phone
groupConversations.detail: Others join by QR code or link from their own phone or computer, with no app or account needed, and each phone works as a microphone.

languages.detail: Ava's help centre (June 2026) lists 23 languages, with 19 more on some devices. Its website says 20+ in one place and 50+ in another, and the App Store says 16. Captioning in a language other than your phone's language needs a paid plan.

offline.text: Mobile only, one person, default language
offline.detail: The mobile apps have an offline mode with somewhat lower accuracy. It works only one to one (solo mode), only in your default language, and not on web or desktop.

speakerLabels.text: Per joined phone; 1-phone SpeakerID in beta
speakerLabels.detail: In a group conversation each person who joins from their own phone appears in their own colour with their name. SpeakerID on a single phone (up to 5 speakers) is a Premium-only beta you must be given access to.

translation.detail: You pick a spoken language and a language to translate into during a conversation; it needs Premium captions, which come with paid plans. Ava's translation article lists 23 languages, but its languages article lists only a few pairs, such as English with French or Spanish.

saveTranscripts.text: Text only, if you choose to save
saveTranscripts.detail: Turn on automatic saving or save at the end; an unsaved conversation can't be recovered. Transcripts are text, with no audio. One help article says they stay on the phone, while the Google Play listing says they are saved in the cloud.

export.text: Email, text, copy; Export on a computer
export.detail: On mobile you share a transcript by email or text message, or copy it. On a computer there is an Export button; the file formats are not listed.

fileUpload.detail: Ava sells Scribe Transcriptions: you upload files and get transcripts made with AI and professional editors. No price is published, and no self-service file transcription in the app is described.

summaries.detail: Smart Recap turns a saved transcript into key points. A July 2024 help article says everyone gets 5 free on iOS, Pro gets unlimited, and it is not on Android yet.

customWords.detail: Vocabulary Boost adds names, acronyms and jargon. The help centre says it comes with Ava Pro, and the pricing table shows the custom dictionary only for Pro and Enterprise.

display.text: Text size, dark mode, floating captions
display.detail: Change the text size with a slider and turn dark mode on or off. Mobile has picture-in-picture captions; desktop has an always-on-top captions bar.

soundAlerts.detail: Sound Detection shows a small alert during a conversation when it hears sounds such as a doorbell, an alarm clock, a baby or a phone ringing. Only in the mobile apps.

phoneCalls.detail: Ava's help centre lists phone calls, FaceTime and WhatsApp as things its mobile floating captions cannot caption.

videoCalls.detail: Ava Connect joins a Zoom, Google Meet or Teams call from the link and captions it with speaker names. Web and desktop only, listed for Canada, France and the US, and part of the Pro plan on the pricing page.

mediaOnDevice.detail: On mobile, floating captions caption YouTube, TikTok or Spotify by listening through the microphone with the volume up. The desktop app shows captions over videos, calls and podcasts.

humanCaptioners.text: Ava Scribe, paid plans plus Scribe time
humanCaptioners.detail: A human captioner corrects the AI captions live, for about 99% accuracy (Ava's figure). It needs a Pro, Welcome or Enterprise plan plus bought Scribe time, booked 6 hours ahead for guaranteed service on weekdays.

signLanguage.detail: Credentialed ASL interpreters (and Spanish Sign Language) over video in the desktop and mobile apps, billed per minute with no minimum. No price is published.

privacy.text: Cloud; trains on audio if you consent
privacy.detail: Speech is processed on Ava's servers, not the phone. Its privacy policy (January 2025) says it trains its speech recognition on audio segments and their text if you consent; an older help article (July 2024) says it uses voice data to learn how people sound, not what they said.

account.text: Needed to host; guests join without one
account.detail: You sign up with email, Google, Facebook, Apple or a phone number. People who join your group conversation by QR code or link need no account or app.

availability.detail: The help centre lists 24 countries, including the US, UK, Canada, Australia and much of Western Europe and Latin America. Ava Connect is listed only for Canada, France and the US.

freePlan.detail: The pricing page and App Store describe free basic captions in sessions of up to 40 minutes that you can restart. An older answer on the pricing page still mentions 5 free hours a month. It is not an ADA-compliant plan.

price.detail: Community on the US App Store, October 2026 (the pricing page shows US$9.99 a month billed yearly), with 3 hours a month of Premium captions and extra hours at US$4.99. Pro, Enterprise and event plans have no public price. Paid plans show a 15-day free trial.

accessibilityFunding.text: Employer or school can sponsor; Ava helps
accessibilityFunding.detail: Ava says organizations often sponsor Ava Pro, and it can contact your school or employer for you. A non-profit discount is offered on request. No government programme is stated.

strengths.text: Group conversations let up to 25 people join from their own phone by QR code or link, without the app, each shown in their own colour.
Human-corrected Scribe captions and remote ASL or Spanish Sign Language interpreters can be added in the same app.
Free basic captions with no monthly limit, an offline mode on mobile, and alerts for sounds like a doorbell or a crying baby.
Runs on iPhone, Android, web, Windows and Mac, and Ava Connect captions Zoom, Teams and Meet calls with speaker names.

limits.text: Free and Community sessions stop at 40 minutes, and Community includes only 3 hours a month of Premium captions.
Captioning in a language other than your phone's language, and translation, need a paid plan with Premium captions.
Pro and Enterprise prices are not published, and Scribe time is bought separately.
The current iPhone app needs iOS 18.6 or later, and phone calls, FaceTime and WhatsApp cannot be captioned on mobile.

sources.title: How does Ava guarantee privacy and safety of my data?
quotes: First, we use your voice and conversation data to train Ava.
When an Ava conversation happens, the audio is fragmented in "sounds", and we use these to learn how people sound when they speak. We don't capture or store what the conversation is about.
To comply with HIPAA standards and regulations, we provide our clients with the option to disable any data storage, as well as any ability to save transcripts.
If you choose to save the conversation notes, they are text-only (no audio recording), and cannot be used as legal evidence or proof of record because they can be easily modified.
In order to deliver the highest accuracy possible for your conversations, Ava needs a high computation power that smartphones cannot deliver.

notes: Conflicts: (1) Live-caption languages: help centre 'more than 23' (22 named + English, 19 more depending on device), website nav and pricing '20+', homepage FAQ '50+', App Store '16'. (2) Translation: one help article lists 23 languages, the languages article lists only EN<->FR, EN<->ES, EN->TR, FR->DE; App Store '16 languages'. (3) Minimum iOS: help says iOS 15.0+, App Store (v3.0.5, Oct 2026) says iOS 18.6+. (4) Free plan: App Store says unlimited basic captions; a pricing-page FAQ still says 'a new 5 hours credit' every 30 days (looks stale). Pricing table lists 'Speaker identification' in Free, but the SpeakerID help article says single-device SpeakerID is Premium-only beta; group-mode speaker names appear to be free. (5) Community yearly discount: pricing page 'save 20%', help article '33% discount' ($9.99 vs $14.99 is 33%). (6) Transcript storage: one help article says saved transcripts are stored locally on the phone, Google Play says 'saved in the cloud' and another article mentions sync across devices. (7) Privacy: help article says voice/conversation data is used to train Ava; the privacy policy (last updated 15 Jan 2025, footer says Oct 2023) says training on audio + transcribed text happens if you consent. Price currency: the pricing page shows both $ and € symbols with the same figures (14.99 / 9.99), so the € amount likely equals the $ amount for EU visitors; I only saw it from one location. US App Store in-app purchases also list '+1h Ava Premium Credit' at $2.99, $3.99 and $4.99 and '+5h Ava Credit for captions' $4.99. Pro, Enterprise, event plans, Scribe and ASL prices are not public (Scribe rates are said to be in 'Scribe Terms of Use', not opened). Smart Recap and New Android App articles are from 2024 and may be out of date (Android may now have Smart Recap / group conversations). Quotes from pricing cards are given as the rendered text (the HTML splits them across elements). All pages opened 2026-10-28 with WebFetch/curl.
